deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this folio. Folio 158v is a printed page of a German antiquarian bookseller's catalogue: page 8 of the section 'Naturwissenschaft und Physik'. It contains alphabetical entries from 'Humboldt A. und Bonpland, Ideen zu einer Geographie d. Pflanzen' to 'Ledermüller, Vers. ein. gründl. Vertheidig. v. Samenthierch.'. Each entry gives author, short title, format (4., 8., Fol.), place, abbreviated year (e.g. 807 = 1807), binding, sometimes the original price in parentheses, and the sale price in Thaler and Silbergroschen. The previous page (p. 7, Gütle–Hudson) and the next page (p. 9, Ledermüller–Mauke) belong to the same catalogue. The latest imprints are 1860 on this page (Koch, 'Dasselbe. 860') and 1861 on the next (Leunis, 1r Thl. 861). The catalogue was therefore printed in or after 1861, despite the bundle label 'MathNotizen1853'. It is presumably a sheet that ended up among Riemann's papers, possibly as scrap paper. No marginal annotations, calculations or handwriting by Riemann are visible on the image. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically. The only mild bibliographic interest is the generic science content of the catalogue (Humboldt's Kosmos, Kant's Naturgeschichte und Theorie des Himmels, Laplace's Exposition du système du monde, Lambert's Hygrometrie, Jacobi on electromagnetic machines). Nothing indicates that Riemann ordered or marked any of these titles.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed bookseller's catalogue (natural science and physics), datable to c. 1861 or later, with no mathematical content and no visible annotations by Riemann. It is routine archival filler or scrap paper.
transcription_corrections: The symbol rendered as $\mathcal{f}$ is the printed Thaler sign (Rthlr), not a mathematical script f. Prices read as Thaler + Silbergroschen (Sgr.).

'Koch, G. D. S., synops. florae Germ. et Helveticae': the author is Wilhelm Daniel Joseph Koch, so the initials should be 'W. D. J.' (as in the next entry, 'Koch, W. D. J., Taschenb.'). The 'S' readings are likely a misreading of Fraktur/Antiqua J.
'Kolhansius, J. C., tract. opticus' is J. C. Kohlhans (Kohlhansius); the spelling as printed may be 'Kolhansius'. Verify against the image.
'Lazare, St., 3 Bde' — in the image this reads roughly 'Lazare, St., B de' and is uncertain; it may read '3 Bde' or a different abbreviation.
'Klimii, N., iter subterraneum' is Holberg's Nicolai Klimii iter subterraneum (Hafniae 1741). The transcription is correct as printed.
Years are printed abbreviated (e.g. '807' = 1807, '663' = 1663, '860' = 1860). This dates the catalogue to c. 1861+ and is not a slip.
